Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations Introduction This Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations is intended to provide a reader of our financial statements with management’s perspective on our financial condition, liquidity, results of operations and certain other factors that may affect our future results. The following discussion should be read together with the condensed consolidated financial statements included in Item 1 of Part I of this report and the consolidated financial statements included in Item 8 of our 2025 Form 10-K . Expand Energy is a leading North American integrated natural gas company, reaching customers from coast to coast across the United States and Canada. As the largest natural gas producer in the U.S., based on net daily production, Expand Energy is focused on responsibly developing an abundant supply of natural gas, oil and NGL to expand energy access for all. Our E&P operations are located in Louisiana and Texas in the Haynesville and Bossier Shales (“Haynesville”), in Pennsylvania in the Marcellus Shale (“Northeast Appalachia”) and in West Virginia and Ohio in the Marcellus and Utica Shales (“Southwest Appalachia”). The recent Twin Eagle Acquisition has expanded our marketing operations across the United States as well as Canada, extending our reach throughout North America within the natural gas value chain. Our strategy is to create sustainable long-term shareholder value by leveraging our advantaged natural gas supply, premium market access and portfolio optionality across an integrated value chain. We continue to focus on improving margins through operating efficiencies, marketing and commercial efforts and financial discipline, while improving our safety and sustainability performance. To accomplish these goals, we plan to allocate our human resources and capital expenditures to projects we believe offer the highest cash return on capital invested; deploy leading drilling and completion technology throughout our portfolio; optimize market access and customer relationships; and pursue acquisition and divestiture opportunities which strengthen our portfolio. We also intend to continue to invest in projects designed to reduce the environmental impact of our operations. Additionally, we aim to be conscientious in our efforts and how they will shape our approach to sustainability for the future and have established the following goals: • Net zero (Scope 1 and 2) greenhouse gas emissions by 2035. • Maintain 100% responsibly sourced gas (RSG) certification across our portfolio. 33 Table of Contents Recent Developments Twin Eagle Acquisition On September 16, 2026, we completed the acquisition of Twin Eagle, a provider of natural gas marketing and logistics services, through a merger with one of our wholly owned subsidiaries. Economic and Market Conditions Domestically, mild weather and strong production weighed on natural gas prices during the first nine months of 2026. Over the longer term, we expect structural demand growth, led by new LNG export capacity, industrial demand, and power demand from data center expansion, to tighten the market and increase the need for incremental supply. We also expect these factors to contribute to greater price volatility. Our hedge positions partially protect our estimated future cash flows from commodity price movements, providing downside protection on more than half of our projected natural gas volumes through the end of 2027, while our collar and three-way collar structures allow us to participate in price increases up to their ceiling prices. We believe our operational flexibility, cost structure, and liquidity position will allow us to manage through periods of price volatility. Elevated geopolitical tensions and episodic supply disruptions have continued to contribute to price fluctuations across energy commodity markets, with attendant risks to the broader global economy. During 2026, for example, renewed military conflict and instability in the Middle East raised concerns about potential disruptions to 34 Table of Contents oil, natural gas and LNG production and to regional shipping routes. Commodity Price Risk Our results of operations and cash flows are impacted by changes in market prices for natural gas, oil and NGL, which have historically been volatile. To mitigate a portion of our exposure to adverse price changes, we enter into various derivative instruments. Our natural gas, oil and NGL derivative activities, when combined with our sales of natural gas, oil and NGL, allow us to predict with greater certainty the revenue we will receive. We believe our derivative instruments continue to be effective as economic hedges in achieving our risk management objectives. We determine the fair value of our derivative instruments utilizing established index prices, volatility curves and discount factors. These estimates are compared to counterparty valuations for reasonableness. Derivative transactions are also subject to the risk that counterparties will be unable to meet their obligations. This non-performance risk is considered in the valuation of our derivative instruments, but to date has not had a material impact on the values of our derivatives. Future risk related to counterparties not being able to meet their obligations has been partially mitigated under our commodity hedging arrangements that require counterparties to post collateral if their obligations to us are in excess of defined thresholds. The values we report in our financial statements are as of a point in time and subsequently change as these estimates are revised to reflect actual results, changes in market conditions and other factors.
